name: Capital Gardens
summary: In Dire Maul's western wing, corrupted growth and spirits haunt the Capital Gardens. Once a park for Kaldorei nobles, the grounds now shelter corrupted ancients, ghosts, and Shen'dralar remnants.

sections.title: A Decayed Sanctuary
sections.body:
Broken marble terraces and twisted gray boughs fill the Capital Gardens. Corrupted treants haunt the courtyards. Ten millennia ago, Eldre'Thalas was one of the Kaldorei empire's great cities. Its outdoor district offered enchanted plants and broad terraces where Highborne sorcerers met to debate and rest.

After the Great Sundering, the enclave fell on hard times. Without the Well of Eternity, the Shen'dralar turned to dark magic to preserve their immortality. The gardens withered, and lingering corruption keeps the woodland from healing.

sections.title: The Athenaeum and the Prison
sections.body: Overgrown paths pass hostile ancients on the way to the Court of the Highborne and the Athenaeum. The library preserves centuries of arcane lore and forgotten treatises. Farther in, the Prison of Immol'thar holds a demon bound by the surviving elves, who sought to draw on its power. That desperate act warped the gardens around it.

faq.answer: The Capital Gardens occupy Dire Maul's western wing, among the ruins of Eldre'Thalas in central Feralas. They once served as a public park and home for the city's Highborne elite.

faq.q: Why are the trees and ancients corrupted here?
faq.answer: After the Well of Eternity was destroyed, the surviving Shen'dralar drew dark fel energy from the summoned demon Immol'thar to sustain themselves. The leaking magic warped local plants and drove the resident ancients mad with violence.
The gardens lead deeper into Dire Maul's western complex, to the Court of the Highborne, the scholarly Athenaeum, and the inner sanctuary where Immol'thar is held.

faq.q: Are there any friendly elves left in the gardens?
faq.answer: Most Highborne on the paths are hostile spirits or maddened defenders. Some Shen'dralar scholars still endure in the nearby Athenaeum, where they barter ancient knowledge or trade for lost elven librams.

angles.text: For night elves, the Capital Gardens' blighted paving recalls Highborne hubris and the ruinous cost of arcane addiction.
The gardens' paths lead toward the Athenaeum, one of Kalimdor's greatest surviving collections of pre-Sundering magical theory.
